title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
description: Given two sorted arrays nums1 and nums2 of size m and n respectively, return the median of the two sorted arrays in O(log(min(m,n))) time.
pseudocode:
1. Ensure nums1 is shorter than nums2
2. Set low = 0, high = m, halfLen = (m + n + 1) / 2
3. While low <= high:
4.   i = (low + high) / 2, j = halfLen - i
5.   Get maxLeft1, minRight1, maxLeft2, minRight2
6.   If maxLeft1 <= minRight2 and maxLeft2 <= minRight1:
7.     If total length is odd, return max(maxLeft1, maxLeft2)
8.     Else return (max(maxLeft1, maxLeft2) + min(minRight1, minRight2)) / 2
9.   Else if maxLeft1 > minRight2: high = i - 1
10.  Else: low = i + 1

steps.note: Initialize binary search on smaller array nums1 = [1, 3] and nums2 = [2, 4, 5].
Set search boundaries: low = 0, high = 2, halfLen = (2 + 3 + 1) / 2 = 3.
Elements around partitions: maxLeft1 = 1, minRight1 = 3, maxLeft2 = 4, minRight2 = 5.
Check validity: maxLeft2 (4) > minRight1 (3), so partition is invalid.
maxLeft2 > minRight1 means i is too small. Move low to i + 1 = 2.
Elements around partitions: maxLeft1 = 3, minRight1 = Infinity, maxLeft2 = 2, minRight2 = 4.
Check validity: maxLeft1 (3) <= minRight2 (4) and maxLeft2 (2) <= minRight1 (Infinity). Valid!
Total length is odd (5). Return median = max(maxLeft1, maxLeft2) = max(3, 2) = 3.
